methodology: Covers the four Mount Washington Valley towns: Conway (North Conway is a village of Conway), Bartlett, Jackson and Madison. Districts: RSA 662 (opened at gc.nh.gov) puts all of Carroll County in U.S. House District 1 and all four towns in Executive Council District 1 and State Senate District 3. State House (RSA 662:5): Conway is Carroll 1 (3 seats, no floterial); Bartlett and Jackson are in Carroll 2 (2 seats, with Albany, Chatham, Hale's Location, Hart's Location and Sandwich, no floterial); Madison is in Carroll 3 (2 seats, with Moultonborough and Tamworth) and the Carroll 8 floterial (2 seats, with Brookfield, Eaton, Effingham, Freedom, Moultonborough, Tamworth and Wakefield). County commissioners (RSA 662:4): Conway, Bartlett and Jackson are in District 1; Madison is in District 2. Races with wards "all" are on every valley ballot; other races list the towns that see them, and wardRaces lists each town's district-specific races. Candidate lists: Citizens Count's Conway, Bartlett, Jackson and Madison ballot pages and its Carroll 2, 3 and 8 district pages; Ballotpedia race pages (Executive Council, State Senate, Carroll 1, Carroll 3, Carroll 8, NH-1) and candidate pages (Burroughs, McAleer, Crawford, Brown); The Ballot Brief and GoodParty.org for county offices and for background; the Conway Daily Sun for county background. Positions for new House candidates are from their Citizens Count profiles (2026 survey answers, campaign-website excerpts or voting-record labels, as marked). Governor, U.S. Senate and U.S. House 1 entries are carried over from Agorri's statewide candidate research (Oct 29, 2026); names and parties were re-confirmed against Citizens Count's Bartlett and Madison pages on Oct 31. Polling places: Town of Conway elections page; Town of Bartlett general election notice; Town of Madison elections page; Town of Jackson primary-day page plus Citizens Count's Jackson page. Incomplete: (1) The NH Secretary of State 2026 candidate list and the towns' sample ballots were not opened; county rosters rest on The Ballot Brief (AI-assisted) and GoodParty.org. (2) Ballotpedia's Carroll 2 page could not be opened; Carroll 2 primary totals are from Ballotpedia's Anita Burroughs page. (3) Citizens Count's Jackson page lists Jackson's U.S. House race as District 2 (Goodlander); RSA 662:1 puts all of Carroll County in District 1 and Citizens Count's Bartlett and Madison pages show District 1, so Jackson is treated as District 1. Confirm on the Jackson sample ballot. (4) Richard Brown sits in Carroll 8 but is running in Carroll 3; Ballotpedia calls him an incumbent there and Citizens Count lists him among Carroll 3's current members, so he is marked not incumbent with a review note. (5) George Randell is listed as Independent/Other by Citizens Count, Independent / D by Ballotpedia, and on both lines by The Ballot Brief. (6) The Ballot Brief gives Carroll 2 Republican Erlon Jones's hometown as North Conway, which is outside Carroll 2; left blank pending confirmation. (7) Campaign sites for Milliken, McGee, Paige, Leonard, Umberger, McConkey, Boudman and Sinkler were not opened directly; Milliken's and Sinkler's quotes are as reproduced by The Ballot Brief. (8) Citizens Count profiles for McConkey (2026), Boudman (2026), Colbath, Leonard, Nelson and Corrigan could not be opened. (9) Party labels: Stephen Villee is Independent/Other on Citizens Count's valley pages and Libertarian in Agorri's other towns; Sheriff Richardi and Register of Deeds Rines are reported on both party lines. (10) Whether Register of Probate candidate Steve Woodcock is Rep. Stephen Woodcock is not confirmed. (11) The 'what' sentence for each office is a general description written for this file, not a quoted source. A statewide constitutional amendment to eliminate the office of Register of Probate is also on the ballot (see county-register-of-probate.related_ballot_measure).
